points.title: 早年求学
points.description: 1842年，马拉美出生于巴黎一个公务员家庭。他的父亲是一位高级公务员，母亲来自一个富裕的商人家庭。马拉美在巴黎接受了良好的教育，先后就读于巴黎多所著名学校，包括圣路易中学和查理曼中学。这段时期，他开始接触文学和诗歌，对浪漫主义诗人如拉马丁、雨果等产生了浓厚兴趣。1857年，他的父亲去世，家庭经济状况恶化，这对他后来的生活产生了深远影响。
points.descriptionEn: Born in Paris to a civil servant father and a mother from a wealthy merchant family, Mallarmé received an excellent education in prestigious schools including Saint-Louis and Charlemagne. During this period, he developed a strong interest in literature and poetry, particularly influenced by Romantic poets such as Lamartine and Hugo. The death of his father in 1857 worsened the family's financial situation, which profoundly impacted his later life.

points.title: 教师生涯开始
points.description: 1862年，为了谋生，马拉美开始在图卢兹的一所英语学校担任教师。这段时期，他开始创作诗歌，并与当时的文学圈建立联系。1863年，他的第一首正式发表的诗作《回声》问世。在图卢兹，他结识了诗人亨利·德·雷尼耶，两人成为终身好友。这段教学经历虽然枯燥，但为马拉美提供了稳定的收入，使他能够继续文学创作。1866年，他离开图卢兹前往巴黎，决心专注于文学事业。
points.descriptionEn: In 1862, Mallarmé began his teaching career in Toulouse at an English school to make a living. During this period, he started writing poetry and connected with literary circles. His first formally published poem, 'L'Écho,' appeared in 1863. In Toulouse, he befriended poet Henri de Régnier, who became a lifelong friend. Although teaching was tedious, it provided stable income that allowed him to continue his literary pursuits. In 1866, he left Toulouse for Paris, determined to focus on his literary career.

points.title: 英国影响
points.description: 1866年至1871年间，马拉美多次前往英国，特别是在伦敦担任家庭教师。这段英国经历对他的文学创作产生了深远影响。他接触了英国文学，特别是莎士比亚和爱伦·坡的作品，并将这些影响融入自己的创作中。在伦敦期间，他完成了《牧神的午后》的早期版本，这首诗后来成为他的代表作之一。英国的经历也使他的诗歌语言更加丰富，融合了英语的表达方式和法国诗歌的传统。1871年，他返回法国，开始在巴黎的多所学校教授英语。
points.descriptionEn: Between 1866 and 1871, Mallarmé frequently traveled to England, particularly working as a tutor in London. This British experience profoundly influenced his literary work. He encountered English literature, especially Shakespeare and Edgar Allan Poe, incorporating these influences into his own writing. During his London stay, he completed an early version of 'L'Après-midi d'un faune,' which later became one of his masterpieces. His English experience enriched his poetic language, blending English expressions with French poetic traditions. In 1871, he returned to France and began teaching English in various Parisian schools.

points.title: 文学领袖
points.description: 1871年起，马拉美定居巴黎，开始了他的文学创作和教学黄金时期。他在巴黎的多所学校教授英语，同时积极参与文学活动。从1870年代中期开始，他的周二沙龙成为巴黎文学艺术界的重要聚会场所，吸引了魏尔伦、兰波、王尔德等众多著名作家和艺术家。这一时期，他创作了《牧神的午后》、《骰子永远不会掷出》等重要作品，发展了他独特的象征主义诗歌理论。他主张诗歌应该超越现实，追求纯粹的审美体验，对后来的现代主义文学产生了深远影响。1898年，马拉美在巴黎逝世，被公认为法国象征主义诗歌的领袖人物。
points.descriptionEn: Settling in Paris from 1871, Mallarmé entered his golden period of literary creation and teaching. He taught English in various Parisian schools while actively participating in literary activities. From the mid-1870s, his Tuesday salons became important gatherings for Parisian literary and artistic circles, attracting famous writers and artists such as Verlaine, Rimbaud, and Wilde. During this period, he created masterpieces like 'L'Après-midi d'un faune' and 'Un coup de dés jamais n'abolira le hasard,' developing his unique Symbolist poetic theory. He advocated that poetry should transcend reality and pursue pure aesthetic experience, profoundly influencing later modernist literature. Mallarmé died in Paris in 1898, recognized as the leader of French Symbolist poetry.

points.title: 晚年创作
points.description: 1891年至1898年，马拉美在巴黎郊区的韦西内度过他的晚年。这一时期，他的创作风格更加成熟和实验性。他完成了《骰子永远不会掷出》这一最具实验性的作品，打破了传统的诗歌形式，采用空间布局和排版来传达诗歌的意义。在韦西内，他继续主持他的著名沙龙，同时整理和修订他的早期作品。他的晚年思想更加深刻，对诗歌的本质和功能进行了哲学思考。这一时期，他的影响超越了文学界，对当时的艺术和音乐也产生了重要影响，如德彪西的《牧神的午后前奏曲》就是基于他的同名诗作创作的。1898年9月9日，马拉美在韦西内逝世，享年56岁。
points.descriptionEn: From 1891 to 1898, Mallarmé spent his later years in Vésinet, a suburb of Paris. During this period, his writing style became more mature and experimental. He completed 'Un coup de dés jamais n'abolira le hasard,' his most experimental work that broke traditional poetic forms by using spatial layout and typography to convey meaning. In Vésinet, he continued hosting his famous salons while organizing and revising his earlier works. His later thinking became more profound, engaging in philosophical reflection on the nature and function of poetry. During this time, his influence extended beyond literature, significantly affecting contemporary art and music, such as Debussy's 'Prélude à l'après-midi d'un faune,' which was based on his poem of the same name. Mallarmé died in Vésinet on September 9, 1898, at the age of 56.

appraisal.zh: 马拉美被公认为象征主义诗歌的领袖和现代主义文学的重要先驱，他以语言实验和形式创新把诗歌推向新的艺术高度，「为诗歌而诗歌」的理念与周二沙龙深刻影响了20世纪文学与艺术。另一种看法认为，他的诗晦涩难懂、疏离现实，形式实验牺牲了可读性与情感，沙龙也形成封闭的精英圈子，使其影响主要局限于文学精英。
appraisal.en: Mallarmé is recognized as the leader of Symbolist poetry and a key precursor of modernism, whose linguistic experimentation and formal innovation raised poetry to new artistic heights, while his ideal of poetry for its own sake and his Tuesday salons deeply influenced twentieth-century literature and art. Another view holds that his verse is obscure and detached from life, that formal experiment sacrificed readability and emotion, and that his salons formed a closed elite circle, confining his influence largely to literary elites.

supporter.zh: 马拉美被誉为现代诗歌的先驱，他的象征主义理论和实践彻底改变了诗歌的表达方式。支持者认为他通过语言实验和形式创新，将诗歌提升到了前所未有的艺术高度。他的'为诗歌而诗歌'的理念强调了诗歌的自主性和纯粹性，为后来的现代主义文学开辟了道路。马拉美的周二沙龙成为当时艺术思想的熔炉，培养了一代先锋艺术家，他对语言的深刻探索和对诗歌本质的哲学思考，使他成为文学史上最具影响力的诗人之一。
supporter.en: Mallarmé is hailed as a pioneer of modern poetry, and his Symbolist theories and practices revolutionized poetic expression. Supporters argue that through linguistic experimentation and formal innovation, he elevated poetry to unprecedented artistic heights. His concept of 'poetry for poetry's sake' emphasized the autonomy and purity of poetic language, paving the way for later modernist literature. His Tuesday salons became crucibles of artistic thought, cultivating a generation of avant-garde artists, and his profound exploration of language and philosophical reflection on poetry's essence make him one of the most influential poets in literary history.

critic.zh: 批评者认为马拉美的诗歌过于晦涩难懂，脱离了现实生活，成为精英阶层的专属品。他的形式实验虽然创新，但有时牺牲了诗歌的可读性和情感表达。一些评论家指出，马拉美的象征主义理论过于强调语言的自主性，忽视了诗歌的社会功能和沟通作用。此外，他的文学沙龙虽然重要，但也形成了一个封闭的精英圈子，限制了诗歌的广泛传播和影响。批评者认为，马拉美的诗歌成就虽然显著，但其影响主要局限于文学精英圈，未能触及更广泛的社会层面。
critic.en: Critics argue that Mallarmé's poetry is excessively obscure and detached from real life, becoming the exclusive domain of the elite. While his formal experiments were innovative, they sometimes sacrificed readability and emotional expression. Some commentators note that his Symbolist theory overemphasized linguistic autonomy at the expense of poetry's social function and communicative role. Additionally, his literary salons, though important, created a closed elite circle that limited the widespread dissemination and influence of poetry. Critics maintain that while Mallarmé's poetic achievements are significant, their influence remained largely confined to literary elites, failing to reach broader societal levels.

objective.zh: 在历史学界和流行文化中，马拉美被公认为象征主义诗歌的领袖和现代主义文学的重要先驱。他的诗歌理论和实践对20世纪文学、艺术和音乐产生了深远影响。在学术界，他被研究为语言哲学和文学理论的重要人物，其作品被广泛分析和解读。在流行文化中，马拉美的形象常常与巴黎文学沙龙和先锋艺术联系在一起，成为19世纪末法国文化的重要象征。他的名言'世界存在的目的是为了在书中找到一幅图画'体现了他的艺术观，也使他成为后世艺术家和作家的重要灵感来源。
objective.en: In academic and popular culture, Mallarmé is recognized as the leader of Symbolist poetry and an important precursor to modernist literature. His poetic theories and practices have had a profound influence on 20th-century literature, art, and music. In academia, he is studied as a significant figure in linguistic philosophy and literary theory, with his works widely analyzed and interpreted. In popular culture, Mallarmé's image is often associated with Parisian literary salons and avant-garde art, becoming an important symbol of late 19th-century French culture. His famous quote 'The universe exists for the purpose of finding in a book a picture' reflects his artistic vision and has made him a major source of inspiration for later artists and writers.

self.zh: 世界存在的目的是为了在书中找到一幅图画。
self.en: The universe exists for the purpose of finding in a book a picture.
